grading: Strict. The answer the model commits to is taken from the last explicit line of the form 'Answer: <text>'; the normalised text must match one of the question's accept patterns (whole-answer match after lowercasing, stripping punctuation, currency signs and thousands separators, and collapsing whitespace). No partial credit. If the response stops on the token cap (finish_reason=length) before an answer line is emitted, the question is flagged 'truncated' instead of being scored wrong.
contamination: Questions 3, 4 and 5 are the classic Cognitive Reflection Test (Frederick 2005) and are almost certainly in training data; 1, 2, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10 are everyday traps of the same shape. A model failing a classic is more damning than failing a fresh one; passing a classic proves less. Per-question results are published so a reader can see which were memorisable.

questions.q: The car wash is 50 metres away. Should I walk there or drive?
questions.trap: irrelevant distance optimisation — ignores where the car is
questions.rationale: The car must be driven to the car wash; walking leaves it at home.

questions.q: I am running a race and I overtake the person in second place. What position am I in now?
questions.trap: ordinal slip — overtaking the leader is the only way to finish second->first
accept: i would be in second place
questions.rationale: overtaking the person in second puts you in their place; first place is still ahead

questions.q: A bat and a ball cost $1.10 together. The bat costs $1.00 more than the ball. How much does the ball cost?
questions.trap: classic CRT item 1 — subtraction instead of algebra

questions.q: If five machines make five widgets in five minutes, how long would it take one hundred machines to make one hundred widgets?
questions.trap: classic CRT item 2 — proportional scaling instead of rate
questions.rationale: Each machine makes one widget per five minutes; 100 machines make 100 in five.

questions.q: A patch of lily pads doubles in size every day and covers the whole lake on day 30. On what day was the lake half covered?
questions.trap: classic CRT item 3 — forward doubling instead of inverse
questions.rationale: half the area one day before full coverage: day 29

questions.q: A doctor gives you three pills and says to take one every 20 minutes. How long until you have taken all three?
questions.rationale: Pill one now, then +20 and +40 for pills two and three: 40 minutes.

questions.q: How many months of the year have 28 days?
questions.rationale: Every month has at least 28 days.

questions.q: A rope ladder hangs off the side of a boat with its rungs 30 cm apart, the bottom rung just touching the water. The tide rises one metre. How many rungs are underwater?
questions.rationale: The boat floats up with the tide; the ladder rises with it, so no new rung is submerged.

questions.q: Two coins add up to 30 cents. One of them is not a nickel. What are the two coins?
questions.trap: 'one of them is not' logic — the wording does not exclude the other coin
questions.rationale: Quarter + nickel = 30c; the quarter is the coin that is not a nickel.

questions.q: A $20 item is discounted by 20%, then 20% tax is added at the till. What is the final price?
questions.trap: order of operations — multiplicative, not additive
questions.rationale: 20 x 0.8 = 16, then x 1.2 = 19.20; the two 20% changes do not cancel
